The loop runs 5 iterations without reducing tempfile.size below max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, then Upload.create_for proceeds with an oversized file, which fails server-side with the same 'file too large' error the feature was supposed to eliminate — the feature silently does nothing.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The loop downsizes in place (from == to: tempfile.path passed as both source and destination), and ImageMagick `convert in.gif out.gif` with identical input/output paths truncates the file mid-read, producing a corrupt/empty image when a single pass would have sufficed. Users uploading large GIFs get a corrupted upload stored and served instead of a downsized one.
records.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (same source and destination path). This diff definitely introduces in-place image conversion for oversized uploads, and the loop can run multiple times. If the underlying ImageMagick/`convert` command (invoked via `OptimizedImage.convert_with`) does not safely support identical input/output paths, this can corrupt/truncate the file mid-operation, resulting in a broken upload being stored/served.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] FileHelper.is_image?(filename) is fed a filename derived from File.basename(URI.parse(url).path) for API URL uploads, which is empty or extension-less for URLs like 'https://host/image?id=1', so the image check fails and large remote images are never downsized. API clients pulling oversized images by URL bypass the downsize path entirely and get the old hard-size failure.
records.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, for API URL uploads the code derives `filename = File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` and then gates downsizing on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. For URLs whose `path` is empty or doesn’t include an extension (e.g. `/image?id=1`), `filename` can be empty or extension-less, so the new downsizing block (`if ... FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`) may not run, leaving oversized remote images to hit the original size failure path instead of being reduced.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The new 3-argument def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) defined after the 4-argument version silently replaces it in Ruby, so every existing caller invoking OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) with integer width/height now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 4 for 3) — or, where callers pass geometry strings, the surviving 4-arg code path is dead. All existing thumbnail/optimized-image generation call sites that pass separate width and height integers crash with ArgumentError at runtime, breaking avatar/thumbnail generation site-wide, not just the new upload path.

Users uploading e.g. a 12MB image to a site with max_image_size_kb = 2048 (2MB) still get a rejection after 5 wasteful synchronous convert invocations, with no indication the system tried or why the advertised auto-downsize did not apply.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop unconditionally invokes the shell/ImageMagick up to 5 times per upload even when downsize makes no progress or fails, with no check on the return value of convert_with. An attacker uploads (or passes via API URL) a file whose extension is an image type but whose content is not a valid image: is_image?(filename) is true, ImageMagick fails or leaves the file unchanged each iteration, and the server burns 5 synchronous shell invocations plus a full copy attempt per request. Chained across requests this is a CPU/process-exhaustion DoS on the upload path, and the upload then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized file since nothing aborts on repeated failure.

FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`) may not run, leaving oversized remote images to hit the original size failure path instead of being reduced.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client-side size check hardcodes 10MB, discarding the SiteSetting-driven max_image_size_kb that the server still enforces for non-images (and for images when the server downsize loop fails). Admins who set max_image_size_kb below 10MB: users are told up-front that files up to 10MB are acceptable, then hit a server-side rejection for non-image files (or oversized images whose downsize failed), replacing a clear pre-upload message with a worse post-upload error; admins who raise the setting above 10MB get files silently blocked client-side below the real limit.
records.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the client-side size limit derived from settings with a hardcoded 10MB: in `utilities.js` the check changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB`, and the 413-handler changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to the same constant. This makes admin-configured limits (including values below 10MB) ineffective for client-side validation and is unrelated to the server-side auto-downsizing logic added in `uploads_controller.rb`.
